# pbs_network_apply (Resource)

Applies the pending network changes of a Proxmox Backup Server node, as Apply Configuration in its web interface does: PBS moves `/etc/network/interfaces.new` over `/etc/network/interfaces` and runs `ifreload -a` (ifupdown2), in a task the resource waits for.

The resource applies when it is created and whenever `triggers` change, after the `pbs_network_interface` resources its triggers refer to are written — reference each of them, for instance with `jsonencode()`, so that any change of an interface changes the triggers. It also notices changes that are pending when Terraform refreshes it, or when it is created — made in the web interface, by another tool, or left by an earlier run —, shows them in `pending_changes` and in a warning, and plans to apply them: PBS applies the whole pending configuration or nothing, whoever made it. To drop changes you do not want applied, revert them first: Revert in the Network Interfaces panel of the web interface, or `proxmox-backup-manager network revert` on the node.

Every apply runs `ifreload -a`, also when nothing is pending, which brings every interface with an `auto` line in line with the whole of `/etc/network/interfaces`: it applies edits made to that file directly, and removes addresses added outside it, such as by hand or by keepalived. `pending_changes` shows neither.

!> **PBS does not roll back.** Once the task has moved the file, the previous configuration is gone, and when `ifreload` fails, the node may run part of the new one. A change that cuts the node off — a new address, gateway or MTU on the interface Terraform reaches PBS through — leaves it cut off: have the node's console at hand, and read the guide _Managing the network of a PBS node_. While the reload runs, the resource waits up to two minutes for an unreachable node to answer again, as a bond or bridge may take half a minute to forward.

Removing an interface from the configuration together with its trigger deletes it from the pending configuration and then applies: Terraform deletes a resource before it updates those that referred to it — unless `create_before_destroy` is set on either, which reverses the order and leaves the removal pending for the next plan to apply. Destroying this resource changes nothing on the node; changes made by the interfaces destroyed with it stay pending — and PBS 4.0.8 and later apply pending changes when the node boots.

Needs `Sys.Modify on /system/network/interfaces`, which an API token may have, and ifupdown2 on the node, which an installation from the PBS ISO has.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# VLAN interfaces from a map, applied once all of them are written: a change
# of any interface changes the triggers, and the apply runs after it.
locals {
  vlans = {
    backup  = { tag = 10, cidr = "198.51.100.10/24" }
    storage = { tag = 20, cidr = "203.0.113.10/24" }
  }
}

resource "pbs_network_interface" "vlan" {
  for_each = local.vlans

  name     = "vlan${each.value.tag}"
  type     = "vlan"
  vlan_id  = each.value.tag
  cidr     = each.value.cidr
  comments = each.key

  vlan_raw_device = "bond0"
}

resource "pbs_network_apply" "this" {
  triggers = {
    for name, iface in pbs_network_interface.vlan : name => jsonencode(iface)
  }
}

# The changes PBS has pending, as of the last refresh: null once applied.
output "pending_network_changes" {
  value = pbs_network_apply.this.pending_changes
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `node` (String) Node whose pending network changes to apply: `localhost`, which every PBS answers to, or the node's host name. Defaults to the provider's `node`. Changing it replaces the resource, which applies the changes.
- `triggers` (Map of String) Values whose change applies the pending changes again, such as `{ vmbr1 = jsonencode(pbs_network_interface.vmbr1) }`. Referring to an interface also makes Terraform write it before applying.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `node`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.
- `pending_changes` (String) Changes pending on the node, as the unified diff from `/etc/network/interfaces` that PBS shows, as of the last refresh or apply; null when none are pending. When a refresh finds some, the plan applies them.
